parts.rationale: Lateral clamshell openings rank ahead of an end cover because they expose the motor_base working region without requiring work deep inside the broad foot. The z-normal option is a fallback that may preserve more of the surrounding rim but offers less direct access. A seam through the motor envelope is not a proposal to divide the motor.
assembly_notes: Provisionally prepare the BODY-side motor_base interface and any required output connection while the BODY halves are open; establish which motor side belongs to BODY before choosing the connection order.
Provisionally close the BODY only after checking that its fastening remains externally accessible when base is attached.
unknowns: Which motor_base interfaces carry stator and output loads, and their actual mounting geometry
Bearing and rim load paths, output clearance, and externally accessible closure-fastener locations

parts.rationale: Explicit deterministic test ranking for PCB-normal assembly: try the generated upper z split first so the Uno can land on mounting-hole bosses. This rank was manually revised from a saved proposal for testing; it is not a new model response.
assembly_notes: Install registered PCBs along their declared normal before closing the upper cap. Other joint and global tasks remain pending.
unknowns: Actual motor stator/output assignments, bearing seats and mounting interfaces at all three joints
Physical component retention, connector directions, support-template fit and wire-tube clearances
Whether either half provides tool access and adequate load paths without cutting an indivisible support; a local hatch or detachable carrier may be needed in a future design

parts.rationale: A longitudinal y-normal opening exposes the proximal motor region along the limb rather than making it the bottom of an end-access cup. The z-normal alternatives provide another approach to that region. The x-normal option is an end-cover fallback close to the motor envelope, subject to retaining the joint collar and its load path.
assembly_notes: Provisionally prepare the arm-side motor_r_arm interface with the limb open; coordinate its output connection with the base-side interface before closing either link.
Provisionally verify that limb closure fasteners remain reachable after attachment to base.
unknowns: Motor retention, bearing and collar geometry, and stator/output allocation between r_arm and base
Limb structural load path, joint motion clearance, wire routing at the seam and fastener access

parts.rationale: The longitudinal y-normal opening offers direct access along the limb to the proximal motor region. The z-normal alternatives test a different approach without relying solely on a deep end opening. The x-normal option places an end seam beyond the motor envelope but must preserve the proximal joint interface.
assembly_notes: Provisionally prepare the arm-side motor_l_arm interface with the limb open; coordinate the output connection and wiring with the open base.
Provisionally check external access to limb closure fasteners in the connected assembly.
unknowns: Motor retention, bearing and collar geometry, and stator/output allocation between l_arm and base
Limb structural load path, joint motion clearance, wire routing at the seam and fastener access
Motor cylinders and electronics are planning envelopes, not verified hardware CAD; geometry and support feasibility remain unverified.
Actual mounting holes, screw and connector positions, tool and hand clearance, strength, and the full motion envelope are unavailable.
Front and gravity directions are unknown; no ranked seam is a manufacturing-ready assembly plan.

The prototype permits only planar two-piece splits. If those cannot provide assembly and service access while preserving interfaces, local hatches, multi-piece cuts or detachable carriers require a future design.
